summary: Risk came off hard and fast. The Nasdaq gapped lower at the open, lost its trailing stop and 50-hour average in the first hour, and bled all session to close down 6.39 percent at 26,743 near the lows, with the S&P down 4.41 percent at 7,381 through its own stop and 50-hour line. Fear came back in a hurry: VIX exploded about 66 percent to 27.77 after sitting at 16.71 the day before. The split was clean, gold caught a safe-haven bid and closed up 0.85 percent at 4,109 while crude bounced 2.25 percent to 90.71 and reclaimed its stop. All of this lands the day before the October jobs report, due Friday morning.

setups.name: TSMOM-20
setups.entry: Trend-follow each board on its ATR stop.
setups.stop: Short the indexes below their flipped stops (MNQ 27,425, MES 7,499); long crude above 88.35.
setups.t1: Index session lows and the next round below; crude the 91.41 50-hour line.
setups.bias: Both indexes are below their stops and 50-hour averages in a hard downtrend, so the systematic read is out of longs and short-aligned. Crude reclaimed its stop and is the lone long; gold is above its 50-hour line but its 1-hour stop flipped overhead. Trade each board on its own signal and size for the wider ranges.

setups.name: AVWAP Hand-off (HOF)
setups.entry: Short the hand-off from the opening-range down-break to a failed retest of the declining VWAP.
setups.stop: Above the retest swing or the opening-range low 27,701.
setups.t1: The session low 26,718, then the 26,500 round.
setups.bias: Today was the clean HOF structure: an immediate opening-range down-break at 14:45 UTC and continuation with no reclaim. Short-only and eligible Thursday (it skips Wednesday and FOMC); the 12:00 to 14:00 ET dead zone applies.

setups.name: AVWAP Bounce (BNC)
setups.entry: A rejection of the declining NYVWAP from below that resumes the downtrend.
setups.stop: A 2-close reclaim back above the NYVWAP 27,090 and the 27,425 stop.
setups.t1: The session low 26,718 and the 26,500 round.
setups.bias: Price is far below AVWAP and NYVWAP, so using them as resistance is the continuation read. A VIX-27 tape is whippy, so keep size small. BNC has no day filter, so it is eligible Thursday.

event.name: October jobs report (nonfarm payrolls) scheduled Friday Nov 6, 8:30 AM ET; today was a risk-off deleveraging into it (no confirmed tier-one US release today)
event.type: PRE_EVENT / risk-off deleveraging into Friday NFP
event.consensus: The October nonfarm payrolls report is scheduled for 8:30 AM ET Friday Nov 6, the marquee release of the week, with federal data still subject to shutdown-related delays. No confirmed tier-one US release printed Thursday, so positioning drove the session.
event.actual: A broad risk-off deleveraging. Equities gapped lower at the cash open, lost their trailing stops and 50-hour averages in the first hour, and bled to the close near the lows. VIX exploded about 66 percent to 27.77.
event.surprise: The speed and depth. MNQ fell 6.39 percent and MES 4.41 percent in a single cash session, VIX more than tripled off its prior-day handle intraday from the overnight calm, and it happened with no confirmed scheduled catalyst, the day before the jobs report.
event.nqReaction: NQ gapped under its 28,301 stop at the open, formed a wide 528 point opening range (28,229.5 / 27,701), broke lower at 14:45 UTC and never reclaimed it, bottomed 26,718, and closed 26,743, down 6.39 percent, below NYVWAP 27,090 and its 28,022 50-hour average.
event.crossAsset: MES minus 4.41 percent at 7,381, through its stop and EMA50. December gold plus 0.85 percent at 4,109, a safe-haven bid, though its 1-hour stop flipped overhead to 4,148 on a late pullback. December crude plus 2.25 percent at 90.71, reclaiming its stop off a 86.61 low. VIX about 27.77, up roughly 66 percent, high 28.18.

risk.openRisk: Index longs are gone, stopped out below their 50-hour lines. Any short carries gap risk into Friday's jobs report. Gold is long but its 1-hour stop flipped overhead; crude is a fresh long off a deep low. The overnight and the open both proved the tape can move a full ATR in minutes.
risk.note: Throttle state DEFENSIVE, stepped up from NORMAL. Volatility roughly doubled: ATR(14) on MNQ blew out to 262.76 from 204.99 and VIX exploded about 66 percent to 27.77, so per-trade size must shrink to keep risk constant against the wider stops. Both indexes are below their trailing stops and 50-hour averages, so TSMOM is out of index longs and short-aligned; crude reclaimed its stop and is the lone long; gold is above its 50-hour line but its 1-hour stop flipped overhead. The long-only momentum edge (E3v2) gate is shut with price below the EMA50 and ROC negative. Treat today's daily loss budget as guarded: on a crash-and-rebound tape the fastest way to compound a loss is the revenge trade. Week ahead: the October jobs report prints Friday Nov 6 at 8:30 AM ET, federal data still shutdown-contingent, into an already stretched and fearful tape, so the Friday open is a high-volatility event; the next policy event is the December FOMC. Size down and respect the stops.

psychology: Days like this are where accounts get wrecked, and it is almost never the first loss that does the damage. It is the revenge trade after. When price is sliding and your stop just got hit, the urge is to flip and catch the bounce, or to double down and make it back fast. Both are the same mistake in different clothes. On a day when volatility doubles and the ranges blow out, the edge is simple: trade smaller or step aside until the tape settles. The market will still be here tomorrow, and there is a jobs report on the way that can move it hard in either direction. If you took a loss today, close the platform and come back flat. Protecting the account is the trade.

fullReport.title: NY Opening Range / HTA OPEN (MNQ)
fullReport.html:
Wide opening range, immediate down-break, close at the lows. OR High 28,229.5, OR Low 27,701, Width 528.5 pts.

Anchored at the 14:30 UTC NY cash open (EST, after daylight saving ended Nov 1). The open was a waterfall: price opened the first 3-minute bar at 28,203.75 and ranged down to 27,701 inside the first 15 minutes, a wide 528 point range. Price broke the range to the downside at 14:45 UTC at 27,629.5 and never traded back inside it. There was no up-break. The 20:00 UTC cash-close bar finished at 26,743, below the opening range and below NYVWAP 27,090.28. Thursday blocks nothing, so BIR, HOF, MID and BNC were all eligible; the immediate down-break and continuation is the HOF (short-only hand-off) structure. Volume is disclaimed on the continuous contract, so VWAP uses a typical-price mean.

fullReport.title: Momentum Breakout (Regime Filter)
fullReport.html:
Gate RED, long-only edge blocked. Price closed 26,743, well below EMA(50) at 28,022, with ROC(12) at minus 6.05 percent, so the long-only regime gate is shut.

RVOL is not available (volume disclaimed on the continuous contract). The regime filter reads red on a hard trend-down day, so the E3v2 long-only breakout edge is out of habitat. A long-only momentum edge has no business firing into a 6 percent index drop with VIX at 27, which is exactly what the regime filter is built to prevent.

Price closed 26,743, below the minus 1 sigma band and near the minus 3 sigma band at 26,734.32, a deeply stretched, trending close. On a one-way trend-down day this is not a reversion setup. The bands get ridden in a strong trend, and fading a crash into the close is the textbook way to get run over. The reversion edge wants a stretched touch followed by a reclaim back toward the mean, which has not happened, so mean-reversion is out of habitat today.

yesterdaysMapScore.note: Published Nov 4 for the Thursday Nov 5 session. The map hedged the two-day bounce holding against a stop loss, and the market resolved hard down. The MNQ lose-the-stop row delivered a 6.39 percent crash, MES lost its stop and fell 4.41 percent, and gold's hold-and-run played out to fresh session highs. Crude stayed below its stop and tagged a new low but reversed up, so it graded mixed. The one not-triggered row was the bullish MNQ continuation, which never set up because price gapped under its stop at the open.
